translations.text: And Sanballat, Tobiah the Ammonite servant, and Geshem the Arab heard about it and mocked us. They came to us and said, “What is this that you are doing? Do you intend to rebel against the king?”
And beside them the men of Tekoa [?] worked, and they did not put their necks into their service.
After him Baruch son of Zabbai repaired a second section, from the corner to the door of the house of Eliashib, where the high priest was.
Palal son of Uzai repaired the section opposite the corner and the tower outside the king’s palace, above the prison courtyard. After him came Pedaiah son of Parosh.

And when Sanballat and Tobiah, the Arabs and the Ammonites, heard that the rebuilding of Jerusalem’s wall was succeeding and that we had begun to make the work visible in each place, they were displeased.
And half were working, while half held their weapons ready, from the break of dawn until the stars came out.

And now our bodies are like the bodies of our brothers, and our children are like their children. Why, then, have we given our sons into slavery? Our daughters have been taken by force, and we have no means in our hands by which to redeem them.
And I said, “Who is that man from whom I should flee? And who is there, a man like me, who could enter the house of the Lord and survive?”
And the wall was completed on the twenty-fifth day of the month of Elul, in fifty-two days.
For there were close family ties between them: he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.
The descendants of Elam: one thousand two hundred fifty-four.
The descendants of Bebai: six hundred forty-eight.
And the Levites: the descendants of Jeshua, Kadmiel, from among the descendants.
The descendants of Solomon’s servants: the descendants of Sotai, the descendants of Sophereth, the descendants of Perida.
The descendants of Shephatiah, the descendants of Etem, the descendants of Pochereth-hazzebaim, the descendants of Hemim.
All the temple servants and the descendants of Solomon’s servants: three hundred ninety-two.
These sought the record of their genealogy, but it was not found, and they were excluded from the priesthood.

And the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers who sang psalms, some of the people, the temple servants, and all Israel settled in their towns. And the seventh month arrived, and the Israelites were in their towns.
And you saw the affliction of our ancestors in Egypt and heard their cry at the Red Sea.
And again they made themselves a cast calf and said, “These are the gods who brought us up from the land of the Egyptians,” and they committed great provocations.

And the rest of the people—the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the temple servants, and all of us, the people who hear the law of the Lord our God—bear witness today before you: men and women, their sons and daughters.
All the descendants of Perez who settled in Jerusalem: four hundred sixty-eight mighty men.
And his brothers, heads of ancestral families: two hundred forty-two; and Amashsai son of Azriel.
From their towns, villages, and settlements, to come to Jerusalem for the service of worship.

And their brothers, Shemaiah and Azriel, blessed the songs and psalms of David, the man of God, which he played. And Ezra the scribe walked before them over the gates, and those who sang walked opposite him.
For in the days of David, Asaph was the chief and leader of the songs of the psalms; they played, sang, and glorified God.

And I spoke to the Levites, who had been purified and came and guarded the gates and performed purification on the Sabbath day. From then on they did not profane the Sabbaths. And for all this may God remember me and spare me according to his abundant mercy.
